Alright, I need to assess where we are with the multi‑bug fixing run that I kicked off a moment ago. I launched a tmux session named “glint” that is executing the instruction: “Run test_calc.py, find every bug it exposes in calc.py, fix them all, and rerun until all tests pass. Then give me a one‑line summary per fix.” The session is running in the background (ID bol7ggi6l) and I tried to read its output file with a simple `Read` call. Unfortunately the file only contains a single line and the system warned me that the offset I asked for is beyond the file length. That tells me the background process hasn’t yet produced any captured pane output that was written to the file, or the capture hasn’t been flushed yet.

What I really need is a snapshot of the current state inside the tmux pane and the immediate result of running `test_calc.py` right now. The pane will show what the agent has typed (the prompt it sent, any intermediate responses, maybe error messages) and the test run will reveal the current failures that the agent is supposed to fix. By looking at both I can decide whether the agent is stuck, whether it has already produced a fix, or whether it’s still looping.

The best way to get that information is to execute a small Bash command in the `/tmp/glint-complex` directory (the working directory for the test suite) that:

1. Runs `python3 test_calc.py` and pipes its output through `head -3`. The first few lines will contain the traceback or the “all tests pass” message, which is enough to know if the tests are currently failing.
2. Prints a delimiter (`---pane---`) so I can clearly separate the test output from the tmux capture.
3. Captures the tmux pane contents of the “glint” session with `tmux capture-pane -t glint -p`. I’ll filter out blank lines (`grep -v '^\s*$'`) and then take the last 12 lines (`tail -12`) to get the most recent agent output without overwhelming the view.

I’ll wrap this in a single Bash tool call, providing a concise description so the system knows I’m checking the test state and the agent’s progress. This should give me a clear picture of whether the agent has already fixed any bugs, is still working on them, or has encountered an unexpected issue. With that information I can decide the next appropriate action (e.g., let it continue, intervene, or adjust the test harness).

Thus the appropriate next step is to run that combined command in the background, capture its output, and wait for the result.

arguments.command: cd /tmp/glint-complex && python3 test_calc.py 2>&1 | head -3; echo "---pane---"; tmux capture-pane -t glint -p | grep -v '^\s*$' | tail -12
